newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ATHLETICS-TIEDTKE RETURNS FROM TWO-YEAR DRUG BAN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-TIEDTKE RETURNS FROM TWO-YEAR DRUG BAN.

text.p: German long jumper Susan Tiedtke made a controversial return from a two-year drug ban with an impressive first leap of 6.83 metres at an athletics meeting on Friday.
Tiedtke, a former double world indoor medallist, comfortably won the women's long jump event with her first attempt of 6.0 metres. Her personal best in the discipline is a leap of 7.0 metres.
South African Sanet Fouche finished a distant second to Tiedtke with a jump of 6.51.
"I'm pretty happy with my performance. I wanted to clear 6.80 at some point -- my jump today just came sooner than I thought," Tiedtke said.
Tiedtke, who is married to former American Olympic bronze medallist Joe Greene, tested positive for steroids the day after she won bronze at the world indoor championships in Barcelona in 1995.
She was then controversially banned for two years under German law, despite an International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) ruling that she should have served a four-year ban.

But the doping cases of former double world sprint champion Katrin Krabbe in 1992, which ended up in the civil courts, have forced German athletics chiefs to reduce bans to two years because anything longer is unacceptable by German law.
The IAAF Council said in Italy on Friday it would not challenge two-year bans handed to athletes from countries whose national laws do not allow more severe sanctions for doping offences.
Germany, Russia and Spain permit only two-year bans.
The IAAF's policy of banning doping offenders for four years will be reviewed at a full IAAF Congress in Athens during late July.
Tiedtke was relieved her two-year wait is now over
"Sitting in the stands watching my husband compete in Paris two weeks ago was frustrating," she said. "I was itching to get back into competition and I'm just pleased that the long wait is now over."
